notes.text: The top passage is cancelled as a whole by two long oblique strokes. It begins pi-torseurs, describes the fibres of a torsor P-j over a set fibre, and reaches the map Phi(t):T to pi followed by alors pi-t centralise. Puis was separately struck before the larger cancellation. H's terminal note explicitly acknowledges the two oblique strokes; its different placement of deletion markup is therefore not treated as an independent reading correction.

The live text restricts an action of the extension/action group to pi and describes the resulting action groupoid: its objects are the set and its morphisms t to t-prime are the lambda satisfying lambda t=t-prime. It then writes component and fundamental-group formulas. These are source accounts; no action-groupoid theorem or identification has been independently proved in this reading pass.

The source says pi-t centralise Phi(t)(T) subset pi and then On suppose T commutatif, with the latter phrase underlined once. It cancels the equality pi-t=Phi-t(T) and writes a live isomorphism Phi-t:T to pi-t. The word centralise is live, and the two uses Phi(t) versus Phi-t are preserved exactly rather than regularized.

The last prose reads d'autres termes on suppose donné, en plus de the set, extension/action-group-ens de pi-ens,. The word de, although donc might be a smoother transition, is what the visible short d/e sequence supports. No comma is supplied after termes, and no extra e is supplied in donné. The page ends with a comma and an unfinished phrase; no continuation was inspected.

The set glyph is not automatically identified with the provisional mathfrak Z described for other pages. Its tau/calligraphic-T alternatives remain open at each occurrence. These alphabet rows are medium confidence and non-consequential; they are not claims of mathematical correction. The first orbit-set notation separately remains uncertain between a low pi subscript and a slash construction.

After the centralised-subgroup formula, the candidate retains the distinct baseline period. Several very small high spots above it are treated as incidental ink rather than promoted into an additional punctuation point. The graphite 20 at the bottom left is retained.

The cancelled top text describes pi-torsors and their fibres, a stabilizer and Phi(t):T to pi. The second reading checks wording, indices, map and cancellation state. The source’s fibre/orbit notation remains uncertain; its mathematics is not used to supply a slash or an index.

The live action-groupoid account, morphism condition lambda t=t-prime and component/fundamental-group formulas were transcribed as written. The new low-confidence shaft/arrow alternative concerns only the tiny connector inside the morphism-set subscript. Its mathematical context does not establish a visibly absent head.

The source’s centralisation statement, underlined commutativity assumption, cancelled equality and live isomorphism are preserved. Phi(t) in the centralisation statement and Phi-sub-t in the replacement are distinct written forms. No mathematical validity check of these assertions was performed.

All four existing remaining doubts are retained unchanged; the indexed connector is a fifth. No existing collation row requires revised evidence or confidence, and no original MARK changes. Pure object-set and extension-letter alphabet questions do not create new material changes.

The final short word remains de under M0699; the source ends in pi-ens followed by a comma. No continuation was inspected. The bottom-left graphite 20 is attributed only to an unnamed hand. No omitted insertion guide or caret was found on this page.
